title: Desk Guidance — Payment-Plan History and the Share Taken by a Card-on-File Charge, Patient Financial Account
content:
The share of the capped amount that a card-on-file charge on the Patient Financial Account takes depends on the patient's payment-plan history, as the patient's Patient Payment Plans records show it:

- when a payment plan of the patient defaulted less than six calendar months before the handling date **and** a plan balance was released within the six calendar months before the handling date, the charge takes 50 percent of the capped amount;
- when the patient has an active or delinquent payment plan **with** a missed installment recorded within the six calendar months before the handling date, the charge takes 75 percent of the capped amount;
- otherwise the share is not reduced under this guidance.

The two conditions are read in that order: a patient who meets the first is charged 50 percent even if a plan of theirs is also behind.

**The six-month window.** A window of calendar months for the card-on-file charge ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it. A default dated exactly six months before the handling date is therefore not "less than six calendar months" before it, and a release or missed installment dated exactly six months earlier is not within the window.

## Points of judgement

| Plan default less than 6 months ago | Plan balance released within 6 months | Active or delinquent plan with a missed installment within 6 months | Share of the capped amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes or no | 50 percent |
| yes | no | yes | 75 percent |
| no | yes or no | yes | 75 percent |
| yes | no | no | not reduced under this guidance |
| no | yes or no | no | not reduced under this guidance |

The records read are the plan's status (active, delinquent, defaulted), the plan's default date, and the plan's ledger entries of released balances and missed installments with their dates.

**Hypothetical example.** Handling date 15 September. A plan defaulted on 20 March, and its balance was released on 25 March; both are inside six months, so a capped amount of 480.00 is charged at 50 percent, that is 240.00. Had the default been dated 15 March, it would not be less than six months before the handling date.
